headline: Criminals warmed the cases at more than 100 European supermarkets and turned stolen cloud logins into million-dollar AI bills, while Britain's National Cyber Security Centre put AI attacks on the country's critical infrastructure at 2028.

emerging_trends.text: Criminals now treat a stolen cloud credential as an AI subscription: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group watched LLMJacking intrusions run models on victims' accounts at more than $100,000 a day, and Glow Labs caught coding agents installing MCP servers out of archived repositories nobody will ever patch.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Stolen Cloud Access Pays the Attacker's AI Bill

emerging_trends.text: Equipment that nobody treats as a computer keeps falling: attackers reached refrigeration controllers in four or more European countries, planted command backdoors on Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced units, and encrypted Synology network attached storage boxes running two-year-old firmware.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Refrigeration Attacks Spread to 100 European Stores

emerging_trends.text: Western governments have stopped debating AI offense and started rehearsing it, with Britain's National Cyber Security Centre naming China and Russia as the states folding AI into their operations and NATO's Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence putting AI agents and OpenAI Daybreak inside its Crossed Swords exercise in Estonia.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Britain Puts AI Attacks on Infrastructure at 2028

topics.title: Attackers Exploit Siemens, Synology, and WordPress Flaws
topics.latest_developments: VulnCheck reported on November 3, 2026 that attackers exploit CVE-2026-58115, the missing authentication flaw rated 10.0 in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices, to plant remote command backdoors; Defused Cyber found exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-81648, an unpatched flaw rated 10.0 in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin that lets anonymous users delete server files and pull wallet credentials; Synology told customers to update DiskStation Manager as ransomware crews hit devices through a bug the company patched in December 2024; and BTCPay Server pinned the hot wallet thefts to instances running version 2.4.1, released July 23, 2026, or earlier.
topics.summary: Four product lines carry flaws attackers are using right now, three of them already fixed and one with no patch at all. Administrators should update SIMATIC IoT2050 firmware and DiskStation Manager, upgrade BTCPay Server and move funds out of hot wallets, and remove the CryptoPayment Gateway plugin until a fix ships.

sources.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
Attackers Target Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw That Can Expose Wallet Credentials
Synology NAS Devices Targeted in Ransomware Attacks Exploiting Patched DSM Flaw
Hackers Exploit BTCPay Server Flaw to Steal Bitcoin and Litecoin From Hot Wallets

topics.title: Refrigeration Attacks Spread to 100 European Stores
topics.latest_developments: The count passed 100 stores on November 3, 2026, with Ireland and Estonia joining Belgium and Sweden on the list, grocers pulling chilled and frozen stock off shelves, and Danfoss, the Danish manufacturer whose controls run much of the affected equipment, drawn into the investigation.
topics.summary: Attackers reach internet-exposed refrigeration controllers and change temperature settings overnight, warming fridges and freezers at Delhaize, Carrefour, and Spar outlets and spoiling food; no single chain reported more than several dozen stores. Grocers should pull cooling controllers off the public internet, replace default credentials, and alarm on remote setpoint changes.

sources.title: Over 100 European Stores Hit as Supermarket Fridge Attacks Return
New Wave of Refrigeration Cyberattacks Hits Supermarkets Across Europe, Forcing Stores to Pull Food
Hackers disrupt refrigeration systems at European supermarkets

topics.title: Espionage Crews Work Ukraine, Israel, and South Asia
topics.latest_developments: ESET detailed Gorbag on November 3, 2026, a Russia-aligned group that has broken into Ukrainian organizations since at least February 2025 with spearphishing attachments and a stealer that erases itself once the data leaves, with about a quarter of its targets in law enforcement and justice bodies and another quarter in local administrations, mostly city councils.
topics.summary: Three regional campaigns surfaced within a day of each other. Dream Research Labs tied DarkBlinders, an Iran state-aligned actor, to the compromise of a high-profile individual in Israel and of a government cloud environment in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq between August and October 2026, and Dark Reading documented PapRAT, which the India-linked group Bitter pushes at South Asian organizations through three attack chains that abuse built-in Windows functionality.

sources.title: Gorbag APT group hits Ukrainian courts and city councils with self-deleting malware
DarkBlinders Compromises Israeli Target and Iraqi Kurdish Government Cloud Environment
PapRAT Cyber-Espionage Campaign Leaves a 'Bitter' Taste in South Asia

topics.title: Harvard Breach Exposes 851,000 Accounts
topics.latest_developments: Have I Been Pwned loaded the Harvard University data on November 3, 2026, putting the November 2025 intrusion into the university's Alumni Affairs and Development systems at more than 850,000 unique email addresses.
topics.summary: Harvard alumni and donors whose records sat in the development database should expect targeted phishing that cites their giving history. The fashion retailer Revolve separately told regulators that intruders reached its online shopping platform and took personal and payment card information on at least 200,000 customers, and Abrigo restored its Sageworks risk management application, borrower-facing features excepted, after irregular activity in its environment forced the platform offline.

sources.title: Harvard University data breach exposed info of 851,000 accounts
Revolve Data Breach Impacts at Least 200,000 People

topics.title: Stolen Cloud Access Pays the Attacker's AI Bill
topics.latest_developments: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant disclosed on November 3, 2026 that intruders who break into corporate cloud accounts run large language models at the victim's expense, a practice they call LLMJacking, with single-day charges above $100,000 and total bills reaching $1 million across incidents Mandiant handled in 2026 at financial services and retail companies.
topics.summary: Attackers monetize a stolen cloud credential by billing the owner for model inference, which shows up as a sudden spike in API requests rather than data theft. Separately, Glow Labs reviewed real AI coding sessions and found agents installing MCP servers from archived repositories that will never receive another patch, a pattern it names MCPhantom. Cap and alarm on model API spend, and pin the MCP packages your agents may install.

sources.title: Stolen AI access leaves companies with cloud bills of up to $1 million
AI coding agents are installing MCP servers that will never be patched

topics.title: Britain Puts AI Attacks on Infrastructure at 2028
topics.latest_developments: The chief executive of Britain's National Cyber Security Centre said on November 3, 2026 that the country will likely face AI-driven cyberattacks on its critical infrastructure by 2028, naming China and Russia alongside criminal groups as the parties folding AI into their operations, which sharpens the agency's earlier forecast of rising attack volume into a date and a set of actors.
topics.summary: The NCSC assessment arrives with its annual report and shifts the AI threat from research demonstrations to a planning assumption for utilities, transport, and health operators. NATO's Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence meanwhile brought AI agents and OpenAI Daybreak into Crossed Swords, its Estonia-based exercise that trains joint cyber and kinetic operations.

sources.title: UK Cyber Chief Says the UK Will Face AI Cyberattacks on Critical Infrastructure by 2028
NATO's Crossed Swords Exercise Brings AI Agents Into Cyber Operations Training

business_politics.title: The U.S. Strikes Qeshm Island
business_politics.latest_developments: United States forces hit Iranian targets on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz overnight into Tuesday, November 3, and Washington described the operation as a defensive measure against Tehran's surface-to-air missiles.
business_politics.summary: The strikes landed hours before American polls opened and pulled crude back toward $106 a barrel after Monday's steep slide, leaving traders to weigh renewed combat against the stalled Qatari-brokered diplomacy. The International Energy Agency said the Iran war has put global liquefied natural gas output on course for its steepest annual decline on record, sharpening the competition among importers heading into winter.

business_politics.title: Americans Vote for Control of Congress
business_politics.latest_developments: Polls opened Tuesday, November 3, in the midterm elections that decide control of the House and Senate, and Dow futures fell while Treasury and European government bond yields rose as traders waited for returns.
business_politics.summary: Voters are rendering a verdict on 21 months of President Trump's second term, with both chambers of Congress, 36 governorships, and dozens of state legislatures on the ballot. The Financial Times reports that Wall Street expects the outcome to set the trajectory for everything from artificial-intelligence policy to federal spending, and the Wall Street Journal flags early-evening races, one Midwestern ballot measure, and the Alaska Senate ballot controversy as the first signals of which way the night breaks.

business_politics.title: Australia's Cash Rate Reaches a 2008 High
business_politics.latest_developments: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate Tuesday, November 3, to the highest level since the 2008 financial crisis, its fifth increase this year, with inflation still running above target.
business_politics.summary: Australia joins the central banks that have tightened since the United States-Iran war lit up energy prices, and the rate path now drives the metals trade: gold futures fell Tuesday as the rebound in oil fueled expectations of further increases, even as the World Gold Council reported that central banks bought gold in the third quarter at their fastest pace since late 2024 on geopolitical risk and doubts about fiscal discipline.

sources.title: Australia raises rates to highest level since 2008 financial crisis
Central Banks Accelerated Gold Buying in Third Quarter

business_politics.title: Apollo Lends a Record $114 Billion Into AI
business_politics.latest_developments: Apollo Global Management reported Tuesday, November 3, that it originated a record $114 billion of loans in the third quarter, including financing for Anthropic and the chipmaker Nvidia, and swung to a net loss of $1.06 billion, or $1.78 a share, against net income of $1.71 billion a year earlier, on investment-related losses.
business_politics.summary: Private credit's exposure to artificial-intelligence infrastructure keeps widening as the trade that funds it wobbles: the Financial Times reported that Marshall Wace and other hedge funds took losses in October's technology correction and bond market turbulence, European semiconductor shares fell Tuesday after a selloff in Asian AI names, and the Wall Street Journal finds investors paying up for downside protection on the sector.

sources.title: Apollo lends record $114bn as it piles into AI financing boom

business.title: City Paper Rounds Up the Food Week
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper published its weekly food column Tuesday, November 3, leading with the Smiley Cookie whiskey that Wigle Whiskey and Eat'n Park have bottled together.
business.summary: The column tracks the week's moves across the Pittsburgh food business, with updates on Wigle Whiskey, Yinz Coffee, Sheetz, Jeni's holiday ice cream, DiAnoia's Eatery in the Strip District, The Drafting Room, and a Great British Bake Off event.

business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled Badamo Family Sandwich Shop and Grocery in Dormont on Tuesday, November 3.
business.summary: The family shop runs a sandwich counter alongside a grocery and a pizza business, giving Dormont a single storefront that covers all three.

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Votes Today
around_town.latest_developments: Polls across Pennsylvania opened at 7 a.m. Tuesday, November 3, and close at 8 p.m., with anyone still in line at closing time entitled to vote.
around_town.summary: Governor Josh Shapiro seeks a second term against Republican Stacy Garrity, who would become the first woman to hold the office, while Democrats defend a slim majority in the state House and try to flip the Republican-controlled state Senate. Western Pennsylvania's marquee congressional race pits Democratic Representative Chris Deluzio against Beaver County Sheriff Tony Guy in the 17th District, and Allegheny County voters also decide a countywide ballot question.

around_town.title: Wilkinsburg Moves to Double Its Wage Tax
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Tuesday, November 3, that Wilkinsburg council wants to double the borough's earned income tax to 2% to close a $2.9 million deficit, and that residents say they learned of the vote only as it approached.
around_town.summary: The increase would take 2% of wages from everyone who works in Wilkinsburg, a borough of roughly 15,000 east of Pittsburgh that has leaned on tax increases and state oversight to steady its finances. Residents complained at council that the borough gave them no real notice of the proposal.

sources.title: Wilkinsburg council proposes doubling earned income tax

around_town.title: Penn Hills Borrows $9.4 Million
around_town.latest_developments: Penn Hills council plans to take out a $9.4 million loan to pay for two municipal projects, WPXI reported Tuesday, November 3, putting a figure on the borrowing the council took up Monday, November 2.
around_town.summary: The money would buy the former YMCA building along Frankstown Road and build a new salt shed for the municipality's public works operation, the two projects Penn Hills leaders have pushed through the fall.

sources.title: Penn Hills leaders look to secure nearly $10 million in funding for major projects

around_teams.title: The Steelers Shop for a Receiver
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette surveyed the wide receivers Pittsburgh could acquire before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, published Tuesday, November 3, and argued the team needs help at the position.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers control the AFC North after beating the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on Sunday, November 1, and their offense under head coach Mike McCarthy has run through Jaylen Warren and the ground game while the receiving corps thinned. General manager Omar Khan has until the deadline to add a target for quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

sources.title: The Steelers need help at receiver. Which one should they target at the NFL trade deadline?

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Works Through the Browns Win
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent Monday's SNR Drive, November 2, on the Steelers' win over the Cleveland Browns, took a call from the team's radio voice Rob King, and broke down the rest of the AFC North's weekend.
around_teams.summary: The show runs on the Pittsburgh Steelers' own channel, with Williamson and Uhler offering opinions the team disclaims as their own. Their Monday installment ran nearly an hour through the Week 8 film and the division picture.

sources.title: Recapping The Steelers 27-6 Victory Against The Browns | SNR Drive (Nov.2) | Pittsburgh Steelers

team_usa.title: Curl-Salemme Sits Out the PWHL Season
team_usa.latest_developments: Britta Curl-Salemme, the United States Olympian who plays forward for PWHL Detroit, announced her pregnancy Monday, November 2, and will miss the Professional Women's Hockey League season.
team_usa.summary: Curl-Salemme becomes the second American forward to step away from the league this fall for the same reason, following Kendall Coyne Schofield's announcement on Thursday, October 29, thinning the United States pool as the women's world championships in Denmark approach.
